We have added a standard HDI indemnity for IP infringement, breach of law, data breach and wilful misconduct, with the usual notice, control and cooperation mechanics.

ops.text: 9B. Indemnification by HDI. HDI shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Site, the services or any deliverable provided by HDI infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right; (b) HDI's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Confidential Information or customer or user data caused by HDI; or (d) HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. The Company shall give HDI prompt notice of the claim, HDI shall control the defense, and the Company shall provide reasonable cooperation at HDI's expense.

proposal.summary: Insert Vendor indemnity covering IP, breach of law, data breach and misconduct.

quote: (b) HDI acknowledges that the Company is currently a party to a web-hosting agreement with Globix Corporation
rationale: No indemnification, defence or hold-harmless language appears in the Agreement, so we have no IP-infringement protection for a Site that HDI designs, hosts and operates. We inserted a Vendor indemnity for IP infringement, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct with standard notice, control and cooperation mechanics.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement never allocates ownership of the Site, work product or the customer and user data collected through it, which leaves HDI free to claim them. We have confirmed that we own our content, the Site and Company Data, while HDI keeps its pre-existing platform and grants us a perpetual license to anything of its own embedded in the deliverables.

ops.text: 5.5 Ownership. The Company owns and retains all right, title and interest in and to the Content, the Marks, the Site as accepted by the Company, all work product created for the Company under this Agreement, and all customer, user, order and transaction data collected through the Site ("Company Data"), and HDI hereby assigns all such rights to the Company. HDI retains ownership of its pre-existing platform, tools and know-how and grants the Company a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense any such HDI materials embedded in the Site or any deliverable for the Company's business. Nothing in this Agreement creates joint ownership of any intellectual property or Company Data.

proposal.summary: Insert ownership of deliverables and Customer Data with Vendor licence-back.

quote: Except as provided herein, no licenses of the Company's Marks are granted or implied under this Agreement.
rationale: Nothing in the Agreement allocates ownership of the Site, work product or the customer, user and order data collected through it; we only have editorial control (5.2) and a reservation on our Marks (6.1). With HDI building and hosting everything on its own servers at its own cost, that silence leaves our deliverable and our data unprotected, so we inserted a Company ownership and Company Data clause with HDI retaining its pre-existing platform and granting us a perpetual licence to embedded HDI materials.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no limitation of liability, leaving both Parties exposed to unlimited and consequential damages. We have added a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, with confidentiality, data protection, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sitting outside the cap.

ops.text: 9A. Limitation of Liability. Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the amounts paid or payable by the Company to HDI under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) One Million Dollars ($1,000,000), and neither Party shall be liable for indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages. "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights. The Company's payment obligations under Section 3 shall not be treated as damages for purposes of this Section.

proposal.summary: Insert mutual liability cap with standard uncapped carve-outs.

rationale: There is no limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages or aggregate-liability language anywhere in the Agreement (Sections 9 and 10 contain only authority representations and boilerplate), so both parties are exposed to unlimited direct and consequential damages. We inserted a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000 with the standard uncapped carve-outs, and confirmed our payment obligations are not "damages".
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

quote: This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns, but no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement.
rationale: Section 10.3 contains no prohibition on assignment and expressly runs to successors and assigns, so we retain freedom to assign to an affiliate or an M&A successor, and there is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right against us. This meets the fallback (mutual assignability to successors); we would prefer a consent requirement on HDI's assignments, particularly to a competitor, but the clause as drafted works in our favour and we are not redlining it.

quote: HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
rationale: The exclusivity granted to HDI sits at the fallback: it is limited to one defined product channel (a self-contained Deerskin Products web site), runs only during a one-year term, is subject to the closeout carve-out in Section 6.2, and Section 1.6 lets us terminate without penalty if HDI misses the delivery date. Section 6.3 also gives us reciprocal exclusivity against HDI, which benefits us. The related restriction on our own activities in the same sentence is redlined under NONCOMPETE rather than flagged twice here.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not pay liquidated damages; a payment measured as half of trailing Net Sales above $800,000 is many multiples of the fees we pay. If an early-termination fee is unavoidable we can accept it capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.

ops.newText: the amount of which shall not exceed the aggregate payments made by the Company to HDI under Section 3.1 during the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date
ops.oldText: the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two

proposal.summary: Cap Customer-payable Termination Payment at three months' fees.

quote: the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two
rationale: Section 4.2 makes us pay a liquidated amount equal to half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 — a multiple of the 30% revenue-share fees we actually pay, and payable only by us (HDI owes nothing if the formula is negative). That fails the fallback cap of three months' fees, so we capped the Termination Payment at three months' payments under Section 3.1 as the sole liquidated amount.

quote: the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled)
rationale: Section 6.1 restricts our own online business by reference to open-ended categories ("products substantially similar", "companies similar to", "without limitation"), runs for the whole auto-renewing term rather than a capped 12 months, and has no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions (Section 6.2 only preserves closeout merchandise). That fails the fallback on scope and duration, so we narrowed it to Deerskin Products, capped it at 12 months and added the development/M&A carve-outs.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need a clean exit on thirty days' notice, and HDI should not be able to walk away mid-term on the same notice it gives us. We have added a Company convenience right with a pro-rata refund and limited HDI to non-renewal at the end of a term; the size of the Termination Payment is addressed separately.

ops.text: 4.1A Termination for Convenience. The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to HDI, in which case HDI shall refund any prepaid amounts for the period after the effective date of termination and no Termination Payment or other penalty shall be due. HDI may not terminate this Agreement for convenience during the then-current term and may give notice of non-renewal only effective as of the end of a term.

proposal.summary: Add Customer 30-day convenience termination; remove Vendor mid-term convenience right.

quote: This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other.
rationale: Our only exit is 90 days' notice and, if we exercise it, Section 4.2(a) imposes a Termination Payment, so we have no penalty-free convenience right; meanwhile HDI may walk away mid-term on the same notice, which the fallback permits only at the end of a term. We added a 30-day Company convenience right with a pro-rata refund and limited HDI to end-of-term non-renewal; the quantum of the Termination Payment is redlined under LD.

quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours.
rationale: The inspection right has acceptable notice (30 days), business-hours limitation, a narrow record scope and HDI bearing the cost, but no frequency cap at all, so HDI could inspect repeatedly. We inserted a once-per-12-month limit as a single-line edit; the absence of an independent-auditor requirement is a residual point we can live with.

quote: This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.
rationale: New York law is our preferred governing law and there is no arbitration provision or foreign venue. The clause is silent on forum; we would add exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, but that is a drafting point rather than a deviation.

rationale: The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or price-matching obligation on us. The only "no less favourable" undertaking runs in our favour (HDI must promote the Site no less favourably than its own catalog titles), which we welcome and do not redline.

ops.text: 4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at HDI's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return to the Company all Content and all customer, user, order and transaction data relating to the Site in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance and data return/deletion on termination.

rationale: Section 4 and the survival clause say nothing about exit: no transition assistance, no return or export of our Content and customer/order data held on HDI's servers, and no deletion obligation. We inserted a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph (six months' assistance at HDI's rates, export within 30 days in machine-readable format, then certified deletion).
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
